welcomeBody: Answer each shared claim that needs your judgment once. Then, for each value, read the arguments on both sides of each issue together and judge the issue. Your answers are saved privately in your assigned account.
welcomeDevice: Use your own device. Unsent changes are retained in this browser until the server confirms saving.
guideParagraphs: This pilot covers one bill, {bill}. For each value, the arguments are grouped into issues. An issue puts together the arguments, on one side or both sides, about the same kind of consequence. You read them side by side.
Begin with the bill overview. Then answer the shared claims that need your judgment. Bill provisions and unchallenged shared statements are supplied as context, without separate questions.
A No on a shared claim means the evidence is insufficient. It does not prove the claim is false. A shared claim marked Yes does not automatically establish an argument.

Each argument shows its supporting paths. If every path in an argument needs a shared claim marked No, that argument cannot give a reason. A shared claim that you have not answered yet is not a No. A path with an unresolved mapping question cannot give a reason until the coordinator settles it. If no argument on one side of an issue has a path that can give a reason, you cannot choose that side. You can still read every argument. You can change a shared-claim answer if your view of that claim changes. Earlier answers stay in the record.

For each issue, decide which sides have at least one substantiated reason. A reason is substantiated when the argument's evidence and reasoning show that the bill would have the effect, and show why the effect matters for the value. One substantiated argument is enough for its side. Choose Support only, Oppose only, Both, Neither or Pending.

Both means only that each side has at least one substantiated reason. It does not mean the reasons are equally strong. An effect on one side is not a rebuttal of a different effect on the other side. Two different effects can both be real. A small effect still counts when it is supported. How strong the evidence is and how large the effect is are different questions.

Choose Neither only when you have read both sides and neither side has a substantiated reason. Choose Pending when you cannot decide. Pending is not the same as Neither. You can complete a value when some of its issues are Pending.

If you choose Both, compare the two sides on that issue only: SUPPORT, OPPOSE or Pending. Choose Pending if you have no justified comparison. Your answer on an issue is not a judgment of each argument in it.

At the end of each value, look at all the distinct consequences you accepted, from every issue. Include the weaker side of each issue where both sides had a reason. Do not count arguments or issues, and do not treat issue results as votes. If both directions have a substantiated reason, choose SUPPORT, OPPOSE or Pending for the value. This is true even if another issue is Pending; take that uncertainty into account. If no issue is Pending and only one direction has a substantiated reason, that direction is the outcome. If no issue is Pending and neither direction has one, the outcome is Neither. If an issue is Pending and both directions do not yet have a substantiated reason, the outcome is Pending.
Keep the stated value and reference person fixed. Use the bill’s frozen version, comparison and evidence cutoff.
Your answers save automatically. Wait for “Saved to server” before closing.
presenceQuestion: On this issue, which sides have at least one substantiated reason?

presenceDescriptions.Support: At least one argument for SUPPORT is substantiated. No argument for OPPOSE is.
presenceDescriptions.Oppose: At least one argument for OPPOSE is substantiated. No argument for SUPPORT is.
presenceDescriptions.Both: At least one argument on each side is substantiated. This does not mean the two sides are equally strong.
presenceDescriptions.Neither: You read both sides. No argument on either side is substantiated.
presenceDescriptions.Pending: You cannot decide. This is not the same as Neither.

strengthQuestion: On this issue, which side has the stronger reason?

strengthDescriptions.support: The reason to SUPPORT is stronger on this issue.
strengthDescriptions.oppose: The reason to OPPOSE is stronger on this issue.

issueStrengthGuide: Compare the two sides on this issue only. Think about how likely each effect is, how large it is, how soon it would come and how many people it would reach. Good evidence for an effect does not mean that the effect is large. More arguments on one side do not by themselves make that side stronger. Choose Pending if you have no justified comparison.
allConsequencesGuide: Compare the overall case for each direction for this value. Look at all the distinct consequences in the reasons you accepted, from every issue. Include the weaker side of each issue where both sides had a reason. If two arguments describe the same consequence, count it once. Do not count arguments or issues. The stronger side of an issue does not decide the overall answer. Good evidence for an effect does not mean that the effect is large. There is no formula to calculate a winner. If some issues are Pending, treat them as uncertainty, not as a reason for either direction. Choose Pending if you have no justified comparison.
valueStrengthQuestion: Considering all the distinct consequences you accepted for this value, which direction has the stronger reason?

summaryDefaults.support: Only SUPPORT has a substantiated reason for this value. The outcome is SUPPORT. No comparison is needed.
summaryDefaults.oppose: Only OPPOSE has a substantiated reason for this value. The outcome is OPPOSE. No comparison is needed.
summaryDefaults.Neither: Neither direction has a substantiated reason for this value. The outcome is Neither.
summaryDefaults.pending: At least one issue is Pending, and the other issues do not give a substantiated reason in both directions. The outcome is Pending. You can still complete this value.

noSide: No argument in this set gives a reason in this direction on this issue.
blockedSide: No argument on this side has a path that can give a reason. Every path needs a shared claim marked No, or has an unresolved mapping question. You cannot choose this side unless that changes. You can still read every argument.
derivedArgument: Every supporting path is blocked by a shared claim marked No. This is a derived outcome, not a new direct judgment.
pathOpen: Open: this path needs no shared claim, or each one it needs is marked Yes or is sourced context. Yes does not establish the argument. You still judge whether it succeeds.
pathBlocked: Blocked: this path needs a shared claim marked No.
pathUnknown: Not yet answered: a shared claim this path needs has no answer yet. This is not a No, and the path is not blocked.
pathUnresolved: Mapping question unresolved: a coordinator has not settled a mapping question about this argument or a shared claim on this path. Until it is settled, this path cannot give a reason.
reassessIssue: A shared claim used on this issue has changed, or your answer to it has changed. Reassess this issue.
pendingSummary: Not finished or Pending. Pending means you have no justified answer yet. It is not the same as Neither.
issueReadings: Read the arguments and responses on this issue
strengthEvidence: Evidence about size, timing and reach
claimQuestion: Does the evidence support this shared claim?
claimNoNote: No means insufficient support, not proof that the claim is false.
comparisonChanged: The judgments changed. The earlier comparison is retained; choose again.
